content.title: About
content.content: Blueberry pie filling is a ready‑to‑use mixture of ripe blueberries, sugar and aromatic spices, designed for quick preparation of homemade blueberry pies. The product is packaged in a sealed pouch that preserves the berries' freshness and bright flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Blueberries are rich in anthocyanins, which give them their characteristic blue‑purple color.
The filling contains a touch of lemon juice to enhance aroma and keep the color vivid.
It is formulated to have the right thickness without additional thickeners.
Blueberry pie is a classic North American dessert, especially popular during the summer berry season.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Blueberries provide anthocyanins and vitamin C, which help combat free radicals and support the immune system.

items.title: Vision support
items.content: Studies suggest regular blueberry consumption may improve night vision and reduce the risk of age‑related macular degeneration.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The filling contains virtually no fat, making it suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Blueberries supply fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Flavonoids in blueberries may help lower blood pressure and improve lipid profiles.

items.title: Berry allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to blueberries.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The filling contains added sugar; people with diabetes should account for the carbohydrate amount.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Lemon juice can increase acidity, which may be unsuitable for those with ulcer disease.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Spread the filling in a baking dish, add your choice of crust (shortcrust, puff pastry, etc.) and bake according to the recipe (typically 35‑45 minutes at 180‑200 °C). The filling also works well as a layer in parfaits, yogurts, or ice‑cream.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened pouch in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep it in a sealed container in the refrigerator and use within 5 days.

content.title: About
content.content: Duck sauce (5051) is a sweet‑sour condiment made from soy sauce, vinegar, sugar and aromatic spices. It is commonly used in Asian cuisine, especially with duck, fried dishes and sushi rolls. The sauce has a thick consistency, dark amber color, and a distinctive aroma with hints of ginger and garlic.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name “Duck sauce” comes from its traditional use with duck meat in Chinese restaurants.
Fruit extracts such as pineapple or apple are often added, giving a subtle fruity sweetness.
In Japan a similar condiment is called “tenkasu sauce,” though the spice blend differs.
Gluten‑free versions replace soy sauce with tamari.
The sauce is believed to balance the richness of fatty dishes by adding a bright, tangy note.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Soy and spices provide antioxidant compounds that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Vinegar and ginger stimulate gastric juice production, aiding digestion.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike many sauces, Duck sauce is low in fat, making it suitable for lighter diets.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: The sauce contains soy sauce, which can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Added sugar makes the sauce caloric; people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Soy sauce is high in sodium; those with hypertension should limit consumption.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Duck sauce is served as a dip for duck, fried chicken, sushi rolls, and vegetable appetizers. It can be mixed into marinades, salad dressings, or used as a glaze during roasting.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the sauce in a tightly sealed bottle in the refrigerator after opening. At room temperature it can last up to 3 months, but once opened it is best used within 1‑2 months. Discard if the smell or color changes.

green-beans-canned-reduced-sodium-cooked.title: Green beans canned, reduced sodium, cooked, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Canned green beans are selected bean pods that have been blanched, packed in a can with a modest amount of salt and no added fat. The product is ready to eat straight from the jar and retains much of the flavor and texture of fresh beans.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Green beans are a good source of plant protein and dietary fiber, making them a nutritious addition to meals.
Reduced‑sodium canning helps lower salt intake without sacrificing taste.
Canning extends shelf life to several years while preserving most of the bean’s nutrients.
Beans provide B‑vitamins, especially folate, which is essential for cell division.
The absence of added fat makes this product suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestive health and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Reduced sodium
items.content: Lower salt content helps manage blood pressure and reduces cardiovascular strain.

items.title: Plant‑based protein source
items.content: Protein from beans aids muscle maintenance, especially in vegetarian diets.

items.title: Contains vitamins and minerals
items.content: Green beans provide vitamin C, vitamin K, iron, and magnesium, important for immunity and metabolism.

items.title: Low‑calorie
items.content: A serving is low in calories, making it convenient for weight management.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Although reduced, people on strict sodium limits should account for the amount consumed.

items.title: Bacterial safety
items.content: Damaged cans or improper storage can lead to bacterial growth.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The beans are ready to eat straight from the can. Add them to salads, soups, stews, pasta dishes, or serve as a side. They can also be quickly warmed in a skillet with herbs for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, keep the beans in a sealed container in the refrigerator and consume within 3–4 days.

content.title: About
content.content: The hamburger slider is a miniature version of the classic burger, usually weighing 30–50 g, designed for a quick snack. It consists of a small bun, a beef patty, a leaf of lettuce, a slice of cheese, pickles, and sauce. Often sold in packs of 3–5 pieces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sliders first appeared in the United States in the early 1980s as part of bar and fast‑food menus.
The name “slider” comes from the verb “to slide,” implying they can be easily slid into the mouth.
In Japan, rice‑based buns are sometimes used instead of wheat buns.
Sliders are popular in tasting platters, allowing diners to sample several flavors at once.
Their small size makes them convenient for children and calorie‑conscious eaters.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: The beef patty provides high‑quality animal protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Beef is rich in heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It supplies vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Portion control
items.content: At roughly 150 kcal per piece, a single slider fits easily into a balanced daily intake.

items.title: Zinc content
items.content: Zinc from beef supports immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: The patty can contain saturated fat, so people with high cholesterol should limit consumption.

items.title: Salt and sauces
items.content: Added sauces and the bun increase sodium levels, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The wheat bun contains gluten; a gluten‑free bun is needed for those with celiac disease.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Undercooked beef can harbor Salmonella or E. coli, so ensure the patty is fully cooked.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sliders are hand‑held; pick them up by the bun and bite. Serve with fries, barbecue sauce, or fresh veggie sticks. For a lighter option, use a whole‑grain bun and low‑fat cheese.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep prepared sliders refrigerated at 0–4 °C for up to 2 days. Frozen sliders last up to 3 months; reheat in an oven or microwave to an internal temperature of 75 °C before eating.
